> Curated papers, systems, and datasets for Text-to-SQL that can recognize ambiguity, ask useful questions, and decline unsupported requests.

Natural-language questions do not always determine one SQL query, and a database cannot answer every request. This collection focuses on how NL2SQL agents detect these situations, resolve them through interaction or additional evidence, and evaluate when to answer or abstain.

[**Explore the interactive catalog →**](https://duyvuleo.github.io/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/) · [Browse papers](papers/README.md) · [Compare benchmarks](docs/benchmark-matrix.md) · [Try the examples](examples/README.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

Updated **2026-11-09**. Each paper includes a concise summary, publication status, public sources, and a verification date. Core work and adjacent methods are marked separately. Resource counts include clearly labeled benchmark designs whose artifacts are not yet verified released.

## Scope

We include work that directly studies ambiguity, underspecification, answerability, clarification, or abstention in natural-language querying of relational databases. We also include selected verification, uncertainty, and contextual-grounding methods when their relevance to those problems is explicit. Generic SQL-generation systems and broad agent frameworks belong in the related collections unless they provide a concrete capability relevant to this scope.

An ambiguous request, an unsupported request, a model error, and a valid query returning no rows are different cases. Likewise, a publication, an announced repository, released artifacts, and independently reproduced results are different kinds of evidence. The annotations preserve these distinctions; inclusion is not a deployment endorsement.

## Recent additions

| Year | Paper / venue | Concise summary | Code / data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026 | [Boundary-Aware NL2SQL: Integrating Reliability through Hybrid Reward and Data Synthesis](papers/README.md#bar-sql)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>core</em> | Trains SQL generation, clarification, missing-constraint follow-up and refusal with mutated enterprise examples, supervised fine-tuning and task-specific reinforcement-learning rewards. Ent-SQL-Bench combines SQL execution agreement with LLM-judged natural-language responses. Evidence comes from a held-out portion of the authors&#x27; synthetic enterprise corpus; response-level clarification scores do not establish successful multi-turn resolution or transfer to unseen domains. | [Code](https://github.com/TianSongS/BAR-SQL) · [Data](https://github.com/TianSongS/BAR-SQL/tree/main/benchmark)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#bar-sql) |
| 2021 | [NL-EDIT: Correcting Semantic Parse Errors through Natural Language Interaction](papers/README.md#nl-edit)<br>NAACL 2021<br><em>adjacent</em> | Maps feedback, a query explanation and schema context to SQL edits, with synthetic edit-feedback examples supplementing SPLASH training. One-round correction and cross-parser tests expose difficulties with longer explanations, multiple errors and irrelevant extra edits. It supports studying feedback incorporation, but does not establish a clarification policy, answerability detection or preservation of every unaffected part of user intent. | [Code](https://github.com/MSR-LIT/NLEdit) · [Data](https://github.com/MSR-LIT/NLEdit/tree/main/data)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#nl-edit) |
| 2020 | [Speak to your Parser: Interactive Text-to-SQL with Natural Language Feedback](papers/README.md#splash)<br>ACL 2020<br><em>adjacent</em> | Introduces SPLASH, pairing Spider questions and erroneous SQL with explanations and crowdsourced correction feedback. Baselines test how feedback repairs a parse, providing a useful comparison for feedback incorporation in interactive agents. The task assumes a fully specified question and supplies a recorded correction turn; it does not evaluate ambiguity detection, clarification-question selection or unanswerable requests. Evaluation uses reference-based exact set match. | [Data](https://github.com/MSR-LIT/Splash)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#splash) |
| 2026 | [SQLStructEval: Structural Evaluation of LLM Text-to-SQL Generation](papers/README.md#sqlstructeval)<br>Findings of IJCNLP-AACL 2026<br><em>adjacent</em> | Measures canonical SQL-structure variation across repeated generations, paraphrases and schema reorderings, including outputs that match reference execution results. A structured-plan compiler is evaluated as a full pipeline. Structural divergence is not itself an error or evidence of user ambiguity; results depend on parsing coverage and supplied database instances, with limited additional-benchmark subsets and no isolated compiler-effect claim. | [Code](https://github.com/XanderZhou2022/AACL2026-SQLSTRUCTEVAL)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#sqlstructeval) |
| 2025 | [SIMBA UQ: Similarity-Based Aggregation for Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models](papers/README.md#simba-uq)<br>Findings of EMNLP 2025<br><em>adjacent</em> | Aggregates similarities among sampled responses into confidence estimates using simple, Bayesian and learned-classifier approaches, with Text-to-SQL evaluation on Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD. The learned variants use labeled in-domain examples and matched sampling procedures. Calibration improvements do not guarantee individual correctness or reliable rejection; the study leaves distribution-shift evaluation open and uses execution agreement for SQL labels. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#simba-uq) |
| 2025 | [The Consistency Hypothesis in Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models](papers/README.md#consistency-hypothesis)<br>UAI 2025 (PMLR 286)<br><em>adjacent</em> | Formalizes and statistically tests whether agreement among sampled generations predicts correctness, including Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD, then evaluates similarity aggregation for confidence and selective generation. Support varies with model, dataset and similarity definition. SQL correctness is labeled by reference-result agreement on the supplied database; consistency is not a semantic proof or a diagnosis of request answerability. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#consistency-hypothesis) |
| 2026 | [Auditing and Repairing LLM-as-Judge Failures in a Production Text-to-SQL Pipeline](papers/README.md#synca-audit)<br>EMNLP 2026 Industry Track<br><em>adjacent</em> | Audits SQL-faithfulness judges against human labels, compares replacements and routes judge disagreements to review. It separates disagreement-enriched samples from random spot-checks, showing why aggregate agreement depends on sampling and domain. Evidence comes from one telecom deployment with limited cross-domain checks; the small head-to-head comparison is inconclusive and gold labels remain tied to the annotation protocol. | [Code](https://github.com/JamesL404/synca-audit)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#synca-audit) |
| 2026 | [Text-to-SQL Models Make Choices Without Saying So](papers/README.md#specbridge)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>core</em> | SpecBridge pairs an open calculation request with two explicitly specified readings to separate computing an answer from reporting alternatives. It also evaluates deciding which readings to answer and preserving constraints after a user pick. Tests cover one choice and two reference readings at a time; simulated users recognize their intended reading, and product baselines are reconstructions rather than live-product evaluations. | [Code](https://github.com/Xyc-arch/specbridge-artifact) · [Data](https://github.com/Xyc-arch/specbridge-artifact/tree/main/benchmark)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#specbridge) |

## Contributing

Suggest a resource or correction through an [issue](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/issues/new/choose) or pull request. Include a primary source and explain the connection to ambiguity or unanswerability. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format and checks.

The canonical records are [papers.json](data/papers.json) and [resources.json](data/resources.json). The indexes are generated, so contributors only need to maintain one record per work.
